books.title: A Little Girl in Old Pittsburg
books.author: Amanda Minnie Douglas
books.desc: A Little Girl in Old Pittsburg is a novel for children set in late 18th century Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania written by the American writer Amanda Minnie Douglas.
about: A Little Girl in Old Pittsburg is a novel for children set in late 18th century Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania written by the American writer Amanda Minnie Douglas (1831–1916).

It opens in 1781 with the news of Lord Cornwallis’ surrender to George Washington as it reaches the Carrick, Bradin, and Duvernay families, pioneers who live near Fort Pitt. The protagonist, Daffodil, is the "little girl" of the title, and the plot primarily is used to illustrate the domestic life of early Pittsburghers. It ends with Daffodil's marriage and her taking leave of the city. The novel is part of a series (e.g., A Little Girl in Old Boston, A Little Girl in Old Philadelphia) that was among the first fiction series for American girls.

This description is adapted from the Wikipedia article “A Little Girl in Old Pittsburg” (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Little_Girl_in_Old_Pittsburg), available under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 License.
books.wikipedia: A Little Girl in Old Pittsburg
books.author_short: Amanda Minnie Douglas was an American writer of adult and juvenile fiction.
author_long: Amanda Minnie Douglas (July 14, 1831 – July 18, 1916) was an American writer of adult and juvenile fiction. She was probably best remembered by young readers of her day for the Little Girl and Helen Grant series published over the decades flanking the turn of the twentieth century.

This description is adapted from the Wikipedia article “Amanda Minnie Douglas” (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Minnie_Douglas), available under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 License.
